titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Translator's Colophon and the List of Kings (Colophon)
part: Colophon — The Translator's Colophon and the List of Kings
about: The colophon of the book: how it was brought out of Arabic into Geʿez, the translator Isaac's plea for prayers, and a closing list of kings, from Bazen to Amda Seyon, as the text names them.

sentences.t: ወተብህለ ፡ በክታበ ፡ ዐረቢ ፡ አውፃእናሃ ፡ እመጽሐፈ ፡ ቅብጥ ፡ ለዐረቢ ፡ እመንበረ ፡ ማርቆስ ፡ ወንጌላዊ ፡ መምህር ፡ አበ ፡ ኵልነ ፤
sentences.l: And-it-was-said in-writing-of Arabic: we-brought-out-it from-book-of Copts to-Arabic, from-throne-of Mark evangelist teacher father-of all-of-us;
sentences.i: And it was said in an Arabic writing: we brought it out from the book of the Copts into Arabic, from the throne of Mark the evangelist, the teacher, the father of us all;
sentences.n: Colophon: a new voice, a translator's first person plural. ወ- 'and' + ተብህለ 'it was said' (3ms perfect, tä-stem passive of ብህለ 'say'; compare ይቤ). በክታበ ዐረቢ 'in an Arabic writing' is taken with ተብህለ (an adjunct right after its verb), so what follows is the quotation; it could instead go with አውፃእናሃ ('we brought it out in Arabic writing') (?). አውፃእናሃ is አውፅአ 'bring out' with 1cp ending -ነ and 3fs object -ሃ 'it' (the book, መጽሐፍ, treated as feminine in this text: ዛቲ መጽሐፍ, ወተረክበት); 'bring out' is the usual word for publishing or rendering a text. እም- 'from' also on እመጽሐፈ, እመንበረ. ቅብጥ 'the Copts'; መንበር 'throne' (here of Mark the evangelist; the text does not name Alexandria). አበ ኵልነ 'father of all of us': ኵሉ + -ነ.

sentences.t: ወአውፃእናሃ ፡ በ፬፻ ፡ ወ፱ ፡ ዓመተ ፡ ምሕረት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ገብረ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወሰጓሁ ፡ ላሊበላ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ አባ ፡ ጊዮርጊስ ፡ ጳጳስ ፡ ኄር ፡ ወአስተተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አውፅኦታ ፡ ወተርጒሞታ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ሐባሲ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ኀለይኩ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ለምንት ፡ ኢተርጐምዋ ፡ አበልዕዝ ፡ ወአበልፈረግ ፡ እለ ፡ አውፅእዋ ፡ እቤ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ እስመ ፡ ወፅአት ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ዛጓ ፡ ወኢተርጐምዋ ፡ እስመ ፡ ትብል ፡ ዛቲ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ እለሰ ፡ ይነግሡ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ተዐድዎ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-we-brought-out-it in-4 hundred and-9 year-of mercy, in land-of Ethiopia, in-days-of Gebre Mesqel king, and-ሰጓሁ (unexplained) Lalibela; in-days-of Abba Giyorgis bishop good; and-(completed?) God its-bringing-out and-its-translation to speech-of Abyssinian; and-when I-pondered this: why not-they-translated-it Abelʿəz and-Abelfäräg who they-brought-it-out; I-said this: because it-went-out in-days-of Zagwe, and-not-they-translated-it; because says this book: those-indeed who they-reign who not-are Israel, transgressing law it-is;
sentences.i: And we brought it out in the four hundred and ninth year of mercy, in the land of Ethiopia, in the days of King Gebre Mesqel, and … (ሰጓሁ, unexplained) Lalibela; in the days of Abba Giyorgis, the good bishop; and God completed (?) its bringing out and its translation into the Abyssinian speech. And when I pondered this — why did they not translate it, Abelʿəz and Abelfäräg (names as written, unexplained), who brought it out — I said: it is because it came out in the days of the Zagwe, and they did not translate it; for this book says: as for those who reign who are not Israel, it is a transgression of the law.
sentences.n: A long unit (54 words), kept whole; the source has no ፤ inside it. ዓመተ ምሕረት 'year of mercy' is the Ethiopian era-name, so ፬፻ወ፱ is year 409 of that era; the date is the colophon's own, and nothing here reconciles it with the persons named, so no calendar equivalent is given. Gebre Mesqel is read as the king's name ('servant of the cross'); the text does not itself say whether he and Lalibela are one man or two. ወሰጓሁ ላሊበላ is obscure (?): ሰጓሁ is not identified (a verb with 3ms suffix -ሁ? a name or epithet?) and is left unrendered. ወአስተተ is unresolved (?): no root is identified; 'completed' is only the sense the clause seems to need (God … its bringing-out and its translation). ኀበ 'to'; ነገረ ሐባሲ 'speech of the Abyssinian' (ሐባሲ, nisba, here collective). አበልዕዝ and አበልፈረግ are not analysed (?): they may be personal names or descriptions; they stand with እለ አውፅእዋ 'who brought it out', so they are the earlier bringers-out. እቤ 'I said' (1cs of ይቤ, root ብህለ). ዛጓ 'Zagwe' as the text spells it; presumably the line meant by the 'not Israel' reasoning that follows. ኢተርጐምዋ: negated ተርጐመ 'translate' with 3mp ending and 3fs object -ዋ 'it'. እስመ ትብል: 'for … says' with the book (fem.) as subject. እለሰ ይነግሡ እለ ኢኮኑ እስራኤል 'as for those who reign, who are not Israel' (-ሰ marks contrast); ተዐድዎ ሕግ ውእቱ 'it is a transgressing of the law': ተዐድዎ the verbal noun of ተዐደወ with ሕግ as its object, ውእቱ the copula. The sense is fairly clear, the exact construction is not (?).

sentences.i: And when it is in the kingdom of Israel, from [the time] they brought it out (?);
sentences.n: Obscure (?): the clause is cut short. ሶበ 'when' + ይከውን (3ms imperfect of ኮነ 'be, become'); the subject is unstated (3ms, whereas the book is feminine, ወተረክበት, so it is not simply the book). እምአውፅእዋ is እም- 'from' + አውፅእዋ 'they brought it out' (3mp + 3fs), read 'from their bringing it out'. How this clause joins the next (ወተረክበት በናዝሬት) is not clear, and no link is claimed.

sentences.i: And it was found in Nazareth.
sentences.n: ወተረክበት 'and it was found' (ተረክበ, tä-stem passive of ረከበ 'find', 3fs). Nazareth is read as a place-name; its identity in this colophon is not explained (?). ፨ marks the end of the section.

sentences.t: ወጸልዩ ፡ ላዕሌየ ፡ ለገብርክሙ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ነዳይ ፡ ወኢትሒሱኒ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ኢያርትዖ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ልሳን ፤
sentences.l: And-pray upon-me for-your-servant Isaac poor, and-not-blame-me (?) for not-making-straight speech-of language;
sentences.i: And pray for me, for your servant Isaac, the poor man, and do not blame me (?) for not making straight the speech of the language;
sentences.n: Isaac is the translator, speaking in his own voice (inferred from the plea for his work). ወጸልዩ is ጸለየ 'pray' in the 2mp imperative; ላዕሌየ 'upon me' (ላዕለ + -የ). ለገብርክሙ: ለ- + ገብር 'servant' + -ክሙ 'your (mp)'. ወኢትሒሱኒ: ኢ- + a 2mp jussive + -ኒ 'me'; the root is not securely identified (?) and 'blame, reproach' is taken from context. ኢያርትዖ is the negated verbal noun (infinitive) of አርትዐ 'make straight', with ነገረ ልሳን 'the speech of the language' as its object, the actor being Isaac: 'not making straight'.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ጻመውኩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ክብራ ፡ ለሀገረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጸአታ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እስመ ፡ አነሂ ፡ ተስእልክዎ ፡ ለመኰንን ፡ ርቱዕ ፡ ፍቁረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ያዕቢከ ፡ እግዚእ ፡ ወአፍቀረ ፡ ወይቤለኒ ፡ ግበር ፤
sentences.l: For much I-laboured for-glory-of-her of-land-of Ethiopia, for-going-out-of-her of-Zion heavenly, and-for glory-of king-of Ethiopia; for I-also I-asked-him the-governor just, beloved-of God, Yaʿbikä Əgzi (?) ('makes-great-you Lord'); and-he-loved (?), and-he-said-to-me: 'Do';
sentences.i: For I laboured much for the glory of the land of Ethiopia, for the going out of heavenly Zion, and for the glory of the king of Ethiopia; for I too asked him, the just governor, the beloved of God, Yaʿbika Egzi (?) ('the Lord makes you great'); and he loved (?), and he said to me, 'Do it';
sentences.n: እስመ 'for' opens the reason. ብዙኀ is an adverbial accusative 'much'. በእንተ ክብራ ለሀገረ ኢትዮጵያ is 'for her glory, of the land': a possessive suffix anticipates the owner, introduced by ለ-; so also ጸአታ ለጽዮን. In this book Zion is the Ark, and its 'going out' (from Jerusalem to Ethiopia) is the book's subject; ሰማያዊት 'heavenly' is feminine to agree with ጽዮን. ተስእልክዎ: 1cs perfect 'I asked' + 3ms object -ዎ, doubled by ለመኰንን; 'governor, judge' with ርቱዕ 'just' and ፍቁረ እግዚኣብሔር 'beloved of God' (construct) in apposition. The next words are doubtful (?). ያዕቢከ እግዚእ looks like a personal name of the governor, 'the Lord makes you great' (ያዕቢ 3ms of አዕበየ 'make great' + -ከ 'you', እግዚእ 'Lord'), in apposition to him; it could instead be a spoken blessing, but then the sentence has no reported speech to carry it. ወአፍቀረ 'and he loved' has no stated object ('approved'? (?)). ወይቤለኒ ግበር: 'and he said to me: do!' (ግበር 2ms imperative).

sentences.t: ወገበርኩ ፡ እንዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይረድአኒ ፡ ወኢፈደየኒ ፡ በከመ ፡ አበሳየ ፡ ለገብርክሙ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ጸልዩ ፡ ወለእለ ፡ ፃመዉ ፡ ምስሌየ ፡ በፀአተ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተመንደብነ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ አነ ፡ ወይምሀረነ ፡ አብ ፡ ወሕዝበ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ወእንድርያስ ፡ ወፊልጶስ ፡ ወመሓሪ ፡ አብ ፡ ይምሐሮሙ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ በመንግሥተ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ምስለ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ወሰማዕት ፡ ይጽሐፍ ፡ ስሞሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ሕይወት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፡ ወአሜን ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-I-did while God helps-me, and-not-he-repaid-me according-to my-sin; pray for-your-servant Isaac, and-for-those who they-laboured with-me in-going-out-of this book, for we-were-distressed (?) exceedingly, I; and-may-teach (or have-mercy-on) (?) -us Father and-people-of Christ and-Andreyas and-Filipos and-merciful Father; may-have-mercy-on-them God in-kingdom-of heavens with all-of-them saints and-martyrs; let-him-write their-names in book-of life for ever-of ever, amen and-amen.
sentences.i: And I did it, while God helped me, and he did not repay me according to my sin. Pray for your servant Isaac, and for those who laboured with me in the going out of this book, for we were greatly distressed (?), I myself. May the Father have mercy on us (?), and Hizb Kristos, Andreyas, Filipos, and Mehari Ab (?) — may God have mercy on them in the kingdom of heaven, with all the saints and martyrs; may he write their names in the book of life, for ever and ever. Amen and amen.
sentences.n: A long unit (45 words); the closing ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is a row of end-marks. እንዘ 'while' + the imperfect ይረድአኒ 'he helps me' (ረድአ + -ኒ). ወኢፈደየኒ: ፈደየ 'repay' + -ኒ; አበሳ 'sin, fault' + -የ. ተመንደብነ is not secure (?): a quadriliteral tä-stem with 1cp ending, 'we were distressed' from context only. ፈድፋደ 'exceedingly'; አነ 'I' repeated for emphasis after 'we'. ወይምሀረነ is a 3ms jussive + -ነ 'us'; spelled with ሀ it is the verb ምህረ 'teach' (compare መምህር, unit 1) rather than መሐረ 'have mercy' (as in ይምሐሮሙ below, spelled with ሐ); 'have mercy' is kept for the parallel but 'teach' is the form as written (?). The string ሕዝበ ክርስቶስ ወእንድርያስ ወፊልጶስ ወመሓሪ አብ is ambiguous (?): it may be the names of the fellow-labourers (Hizb Kristos, 'people of Christ'; Andreyas; Filipos; Mehari Ab, 'merciful Father'), which would give ይምሐሮሙ 'may he have mercy on them' its referent; or Christ's people, Andrew, Philip and the Father as further subjects. The verb agrees only with አብ (singular). The second reading is not taken. ይጽሐፍ is the active 3ms jussive of ጸሐፈ 'write': 'let him write their names' (subject understood, God); a passive would be ይትጻሐፍ. 'Book of life' recalls Philippians 4:3 and Revelation 3:5. ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for ever and ever'; ኵሎሙ 'all of them' (ኵሉ + -ሙ).

sentences.i: And after our Saviour was born: these are the kings.
sentences.n: A new section: a list of kings. እምድኅረ 'after' + ተወልደ 'was born' (tä-stem passive of ወለደ), subject መድኀኒነ 'our Saviour' (መድኀኒ + -ነ). እሉ is the plural 'these', ነገሥት 'kings' (broken plural of ንጉሥ). The units that follow end at ፤, mostly one name each (some hold two or three: አብርሃ ወአጽብሐ, አርፍድ ወአምሲ); the list ends at ፨. The Geʿez spellings are kept exactly; the English forms are conventional spellings of the names, and no name is given a sense unless a note says so.
King's name; the sense, if any, is not claimed.

Name; spelling as printed.

Name. ወድም could be ወ- 'and' + ድም (two kings), but a later unit has ውድም አርዓድ with the same consonants in one name, and here no ወ- joins two names with አኀው 'brothers' as in the pairs above; so ወድም is read as one name-element (?) and the unit as one name, 'Anbasa Wudem'. አንበሳ is also the ordinary word 'lion'; no sense is claimed for the name.
Name. ድል and ነአድ are given as printed; ድል is also a word ('victory'), but no sense is claimed for the name. The ፨ closes this list; the text then goes on.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ተሀይደ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ለሕዝብ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ እምነገደ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወሕዝበ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him was-taken-away (?) kingdom to-people who not-are from-tribe-of David and-people-of Israel;
sentences.i: And after him the kingdom was taken away (?) to a people who were not of the tribe of David and the people of Israel;
sentences.n: ወእምድኅሬሁ 'and after him' (እምድኅረ + -ሁ). ተሀይደ is uncertain (?): the house reading is 'was taken away' (3ms perfect passive, stem uncertain), possibly from a root ሀየደ 'go, depart' (not checked against Dillmann here); 'passed' would be the sense the clause needs. ለሕዝብ 'to a people'; እለ ኢኮኑ 'who are not' (ኮነ negated). ነገድ 'tribe', ዳዊት David. The people meant are not named here; they are presumably those of the colophon's 'not Israel' reasoning above (?).

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ አነ ፡ አቀንኦሙ ፡ በዘኢኮነ ፡ ሕዝብ ።
sentences.l: As said God: I I-will-make-them-jealous with-that-which-not-is people.
sentences.i: As God said: I will make them jealous with what is no people.
sentences.n: A quotation, rebuilt from the grammar: Deuteronomy 32:21 (also quoted at Romans 10:19), put in God's mouth by the text. አቀንኦሙ is አቀነአ (causative of ቀነአ 'be jealous') 1cs imperfect with 3mp -ሙ 'them'; በዘ ኢኮነ ሕዝብ 'with that which is not a people'.

sentences.i: And after him he gave back [it] to them;
sentences.n: አግብአ is the causative of ገብአ 'return': 'brought back, gave back'; ሎሙ 'to them'. What is given back (the kingdom, presumably) and the subject are understood, not stated (?); the subject may be the king named in the next unit.

Name. The ኵ here also stands for 'ku' (as in ኵሉ), so ይኵኖ may be ይኩኖ, from the jussive ይኩን 'may it be' + -ኦ 'to him' ('may God be to him'?), but this is a guess (?) and no sense is claimed. It is not a form of ኰነ. Placed after አግብአ ሎሙ, the name may be that of the one who restored (?); nothing more is said about him in the text.

Name. ያግባ is not a form I can identify: a jussive of አግብአ would be ያግብእ, which does not match. Any link with አግብአ in the sentence above is a guess (?); the name is taken as a name only, with ጽዮን 'Zion' as its second element, and no sense is claimed.
Name; ባሕር is also the word 'sea'; ሰገድ as above; no sense claimed.
Name; ሕዝበ has the form 'people of' (construct) + አርዓድ; no sense claimed.
Name; ቅድመ has the form of 'before' (preposition/construct) + ሰገድ; no sense claimed.
Name; as the earlier Jan Segad.
Name; spelling as printed (ውድም, with ው).
Name; read word by word, ዓምደ 'pillar of' (construct of ዓምድ) + ጽዮን 'Zion', the usual form of this name. The nine ፨ close the colophon.
